disclaimer: Drafted from real, current Polish law, retrieved via web search against official/reputable secondary sources describing the Polish Act of 10 May 2018 on the Protection of Personal Data and UOKiK consumer-protection enforcement, as an engineering starting point. This is NOT verified legal compliance and NOT a substitute for review by qualified Polish legal counsel. Scope: National("PL") — this file covers ONLY Poland-specific law that supplements the EU-wide baseline already covered in national/eu.json (GDPR, DSA, UCPD, EU AI Act) — it does not duplicate that content. Every rule's action is a conservative, generic engineering policy, not a legal conclusion. This content will age — re-verify before relying on it.

rules.source: Polish Act of 10 May 2018 on the Protection of Personal Data — fixes the national age of digital consent (GDPR Article 8) at 16, matching the GDPR default rather than lowering it; establishes UODO (Urząd Ochrony Danych Osobowych) as the supervisory authority. https://www.recordinglaw.com/world-laws/world-data-privacy-laws/poland-data-privacy-laws/

Poland's August 2024 implementation of Directive (EU) 2020/1828 on representative actions — allows authorized consumer organizations to bring collective actions on behalf of consumers, including for GDPR violations; UOKiK (Office of Competition and Consumer Protection) separately enforces unfair market practices and is developing tooling to detect dark patterns in online commerce. https://www.dataguidance.com/jurisdiction/poland

Act on Artificial Intelligence Systems (Ustawa o systemach sztucznej inteligencji) — adopted by Parliament 3 July 2026, signed by the President 24 July 2026, published in the 2026 Journal of Laws 27 July 2026, in force 11 August 2026 — https://www.regulatoryai.eu/ai-act-poland/
rules.retrieved_snippet: National implementing legislation for the EU AI Act — genuinely national-specific, not a restatement of eu.json's AI Act rules: creates the Commission for the Development and Safety of AI (KRiBSI), nested within the Ministry of Digital Affairs, as Poland's single market-surveillance authority (one of only two EU states, with Lithuania, to designate a sole authority), with real inspection, sanction, and regulatory-sandbox powers. From 2 August 2026, businesses in Poland must also comply with EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations (chatbots, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, deepfakes).

rules.source: Act on ensuring compliance with digital accessibility requirements (implementing the European Accessibility Act) — entered into force June 2025; earlier Act on Digital Accessibility of Websites and Mobile Applications of Public Entities of 4 April 2019 (transposing the EU Web Accessibility Directive) — https://www.w3.org/WAI/policies/poland/
rules.retrieved_snippet: The 2019 Act requires Polish public-sector websites/apps to meet WCAG 2.1 AA and publish an accessibility statement, with fines from PLN 5,000 to 100,000. The 2025 EAA-implementing Act extends WCAG 2.1 AA obligations to many private-sector companies as well, effective 28 June 2025 — genuinely broader than the EU-wide baseline and not yet covered in eu.json.
